the dynamic response of a building is strongly influenced by the subsoil and foundation, and that this influence cannot be disregarded in any case.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SSI is an essential component to be considered in the analysis of the dynamic behaviour of historical masonry structures.
SSI is an important issue to consider in the analysis of existing historical masonry buildings, and it can be introduced in the numerical models by a simplified approach.
the SSI should always be included when the dynamic behaviour of historical masonry buildings is investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of FE model is able to predict the experimental results in a reliable way, and that the subsoil effect can be properly introduced in FE models by using a simple approach.
the SSI effects can be neglected only if the building is very stiff in respect to the soil and the soil is not very stiff.
